title: Pricing Harness — Scenario Compare Request
description: Input to the Scenario Compare orchestration layer (docs/features/scenario_compare/SPEC.md). NOT a client_input variant and NOT nested inside analysis_result.schema.json — Scenario Compare spans multiple derived Client Inputs (one per scenario), not one (SPEC.md section 19). Overrides are grouped by target kind and addressed by component_id/item_id (SPEC.md section 4) — never by array index.

base_input.description: A full, valid client_input — same schema as every other mode consumes, no new shape. Every scenario is a deep copy of this document with its own overrides applied (SPEC.md section 2).

baseline_scenario_id.description: Must match exactly one scenarios[].scenario_id (SPEC.md section 13). Required, never inferred from list position.

scenarios.description: SPEC.md section 16: Python core enforces only the >=2 lower bound, no upper bound.

overrides.description: Every group is optional; omitting a group or a field within it means 'keep base_input's value' (SPEC.md section 5). A field present with value null means UNKNOWN, identical to a blank field on a hand-authored client_input — omitted and explicit-null are never conflated.

component_override.description: component_id addresses an existing product.price_components[].component_id in base_input (checked at Scenario Compare preflight, not by this schema alone — a schema-valid override can still name a component_id that doesn't exist in a particular base_input). Never overridable here: cost_category-equivalent fields, or the component_id itself (that IS the address, not a value).

cost_item_override.description: item_id addresses an existing costs.items[].item_id in base_input (checked at preflight). Never overridable here: cost_category, basis, applies_to_component, allocation_rule, or item_id itself — changing any of those would redefine what the item means, not just its value (SPEC.md section 4).
